entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill
comments: # The skill seam itself: ctx.skills, a scope-layered registry of named
# skill PROVIDERS — the same Definition → Provider → Consumer shape as
# ctx.subagents.  It owns no skill source and renders no model-facing
# surface: providers register catalogs, consumers read them.
# No config (collectCacheMaxEntries defaults to 128).

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem
comments: # Provider "filesystem" (default providerName): scans the project roots
# (.dsh/skills, .agents/skills at the nearest .git ancestor), then
# customSkillDirs, then the user roots (~/.dsh/skills, ~/.agents/skills)
# for <name>/SKILL.md bundles and flat <name>.md files.  The chokidar
# watch (default on) invalidates the provider so the next pre-step
# republishes a changed catalog.  inject [skills] — satisfied above;
# all defaults kept.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill
comments: # Consumer: emits the durable <available_skills> catalog message before
# the first request (append-only complete replacement when membership,
# descriptions, or tool visibility change) and registers the `skill`
# loader tool, whose result is the canonical <skill_content> block.
# inject [agents, tools, skills] — all present in this graph.
# No config (catalogDescriptionMaxLength defaults to 500).

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-badge
comments: # DISABLED — optional bundled provider contributing the fixed `dsh-badge`
# skill (official "powered by dsh" Markdown snippets plus the packaged
# PNG as resource base).  The upstream CLI composition ships this row
# disabled: true as an explicit opt-in, and the same choice is kept
# here; enable it to see a guaranteed built-in skill enter the catalog.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver
comments: # The runtime that makes goal mode autonomous: at whole-agent idle, an
# active, armed goal with remaining capacity is continued as sequential
# retained <goal_round> prompts, each admitted only after a
# sessions.flush() durability checkpoint.  inject [agents, goals,
# sessions] — goals comes from the stateful-task closure above.  No
# config BY DESIGN: the round cap lives in the goal definition and the
# blocked threshold in dsh-tool-goal, so the driver cannot diverge
# from either.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions
entries.configYaml:
config:
    # REQUIRED, no schema default: per-session render budget for the whole
    # injected instruction chain — each deployment must make this
    # prompt-budget choice explicitly.  Broader files are dropped whole
    # before the most-specific file is truncated.
    maxBytes: 32768
comments: # AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md loader (the roadmap's "reads AGENTS.md"): folds
# the user-global ($DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md) plus project instruction chain
# into durable history at the first pre-step, then discovers nested
# files after successful read/write/edit tool calls — additions,
# replacements, and removal notices.  Reads go through the optional
# ctx.fs (no static inject, so providerless trees still boot); here
# the L5 sandboxed fs serves them.  Defaults kept: candidates
# AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md + .local overlays, maxSourceBytes 1 MiB,
# projectRootMarkers ['.git'].

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-schedule
comments: # Durable reminders hung on the session event log: schedule_create /
# schedule_list / schedule_delete tools, installed on root agents
# created after this plugin loads.  schedule/change events are the only
# authority — timers, tool values, and due-reminder follow-ups are
# disposable projections, so replay reconstructs every reminder.
# inject [agents, sessions, tools, sessionPersistence] — persistence
# comes from the L2 JSONL backend, and the static inject makes a
# missing persistence service a composition error.  No config.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-str-replace-editor
comments: # Model-facing surgical editor: str_replace_editor (view / create /
# str_replace / insert) over ctx.fs — one unique literal match
# required, no regex, no replace_all.  inject [tools, fs]: fs is the
# sandboxed provider from L5, and every mutation routes through
# fs/write-intent / fs/edit-intent, so the sandbox policy and the L6
# approval gate apply unchanged.  Defaults kept (maxOutputChars
# 16000, package tool description).
